clue.text: The new stadium designed for West Ham United, perhaps?

definitions.text: The new stadium designed for West Ham United, perhaps?

parts.words: The new stadium designed for West Ham United, perhaps?
parts.note: the letters of 'the new stadium' rearranged spell out 'West Ham United', so the whole phrase is an example of this kind of wordplay

explanation.surface: A question about the purpose-built ground a London football club moved into.
explanation.walkthrough: West Ham United is a London football club that moved into a new stadium, so the surface reads as sports news. The cryptic point is that 'the new stadium' and 'West Ham United' contain exactly the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A word or phrase made by rearranging the letters of another is the term named, and these two phrases are such a pair.

clue.text: Notice golfer finally, short distance off course

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement

indicators.note: finally takes the final letter of the word golfer

parts.note: one foot, written I (Roman one) and FT (foot), is a short distance

explanation.surface: A golfer's last shot lands just a little way off the fairway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short distance' is I FT, one foot: Roman numeral I and the imperial abbreviation FT.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat drifting without control is no longer on its route, so the word means having gone astray.

clue.text: Feature performance involving special source of expertise

indicators.note: involving means the word for performance surrounds the other letters

parts.note: an act is a performance on stage

indicators.note: source of takes the opening letter of expertise

explanation.surface: A highlight of a show draws on a special kind of know-how.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of' means the first letter of expertise, and 'involving' says the performance word wraps round the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A feature or facet of something is one particular side of it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Dietary supplement from which a queen benefits?

definitions.text: Dietary supplement from which a queen benefits?

parts.words: Dietary supplement from which a queen benefits?
parts.note: worker bees feed a special secretion to larvae destined to become queens, and it is also sold as a health supplement

explanation.surface: A question about which health product a monarch might take.
explanation.walkthrough: The queen is not a monarch but a queen bee, raised on this secretion from worker bees.
explanation.definitionFit: The bee secretion that turns a larva into a queen is sold in health shops as a supplement.

clue.text: Intended food must contain new ingredient

indicators.note: must contain means the word for food holds the extra letter inside it

parts.note: meat is food, especially for a carnivore
N is the abbreviation for new, here an ingredient added inside

explanation.surface: A recipe was supposed to include something novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must contain' puts N inside MEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that was planned or designed to happen was purposed, the past participle of this verb.

clue.text: Floral wreath kid is upset to put down

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so the word for kid is written backwards

parts.note: to kid is to tease or rag someone
to put down an aircraft is to land it

explanation.surface: A child is distressed about having to lay down a ring of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' looks like a child but is the verb to tease, RAG; 'is upset' turns it into GAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring of flowers worn or hung as decoration is the standard sense of this word.

clue.text: Respects detailed environmental articles husband disregarded

indicators.note: detailed here means de-tailed, losing the last letter

parts.note: green means environmentally friendly

indicators.note: disregarded means the abbreviation for husband is left out

parts.note: articles are things or items

explanation.surface: A report reads like a detailed study of green products minus a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' cuts the tail off GREEN to give GREE; 'disregarded' takes H out of THINGS, leaving TINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sending your respects means passing on good wishes, as in a formal salutation.

clue.text: Rough game is supported by lowest social classes

indicators.note: is supported by means in this down answer the first part sits on top of the second

parts.note: RU is rugby union
D and E are the lowest grades in the British socio-economic classification

explanation.surface: A rough sport is played and followed by the working class.
explanation.walkthrough: In British market-research grades, D and E are the lowest social groups.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough in the sense of crude or unrefined is a common synonym of this word.

clue.text: Creations modelled from trash, mostly?

indicators.note: modelled means shaped into a new form, so the letters are rearranged
mostly means most of the word trash, dropping its final letter

explanation.surface: Artworks fashioned out of rubbish, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops H from trash, and 'modelled' rearranges FROM TRAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Painting, sculpture and music are examples of creative disciplines, a loose sense of creations.

clue.text: Slow people boring when crossing road

parts.note: boring means dull

indicators.note: crossing means the word for when spans the road abbreviation, holding it inside

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Slow pedestrians are tedious when walking across the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' says the word for when straddles the road abbreviation; 'Slow' is not about walking speed but about wits.
explanation.definitionFit: Slow-witted people are called dimwits or dunces, and this word is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Compensate occasionally greedy, grasping old man

indicators.note: grasping means the alternate letters hold the father figure inside them
occasionally means taking only some letters of greedy, here every other one

parts.note: old man is informal for father, PA

explanation.surface: Someone is told to make amends from time to time to a grabbing elderly gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes the even letters of greedy, and 'grasping' says they hold the father figure inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay back or make amends for a loss is to compensate, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Dance a lot when tipsy, according to accounts

indicators.note: a tipsy person staggers about, so the letters of the fodder are jumbled

explanation.surface: Reports say someone dances a great deal once they have had a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when tipsy' rearranges the letters of DANCE A LOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Evidence based on stories people tell rather than proper study is described this way, so it fits a phrase about relying on reports.

clue.text: Encourage female to abandon a facelift — it melted!

indicators.note: something melted has lost its shape, so the remaining letters are rearranged
to abandon means one letter leaves the fodder before it is rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman is urged to give up on cosmetic surgery because it collapsed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to abandon' removes an F from A FACELIFT IT, and 'melted' rearranges what is left, AACELIFTIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a process easier or help it along is to encourage it, a close synonym.

clue.text: Scrap audio tapes to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An instruction to throw away some recordings, but only partly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' looks like a verb telling you to discard the tapes; it is the noun meaning a tiny bit.
explanation.definitionFit: A very small amount or jot is what this Greek letter name means in English idiom, as in 'not one bit'.

clue.text: Revolutionary children's entertainer?

definitions.meaning: indirect, going in circles, as in a circuitous route
a playground ride that spins children round

explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests political upheaval but means turning in circles.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinning playground ride amuses children, and the same word describes something indirect.

clue.text: Knowledgeable about water sources?

definitions.meaning: having plenty of facts at your fingertips
read cryptically, having information about wells, the holes dug to draw up water

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into its parts: informed about wells.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who knows a lot about current matters is described with this compound adjective.

clue.text: Spaniard visits solitary individuals, capitalists

indicators.note: visits means the Spaniard goes inside the word for solitary people

parts.note: loners are people who keep to themselves
Don is a Spanish title for a gentleman, so a Spaniard

explanation.surface: A Spanish man calls on recluses who are financiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capitalists' looks like financiers; it means people from the capital city, London.
explanation.definitionFit: People from the British capital are residents of London, so they are capital-dwellers.

clue.text: Sweet smell, it's apparently returning somewhat

indicators.note: returning says the hidden letters are read backwards
somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A pleasant aroma seems to be coming back a bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' picks ELLITSAP out of 'smell, it's apparently', and 'returning' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A small medicated or flavoured lozenge is a kind of sweet or candy.

clue.text: Affectionate expression boy uses freely about student

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters surround the extra one
freely means the letters are arranged without restriction

parts.note: L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A lad uses a fond phrase liberally around a pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' rearranges BOY USES, and 'about' puts it around L.
explanation.definitionFit: Said kindly when someone sneezes, this phrase is a warm wish, so an affectionate expression.

clue.text: Traditional chorus in England, say, rendered around middle of July

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters go round the central letters of the month
rendered means performed in a new version, so the letters are rearranged
middle of takes the two central letters of the month name

explanation.surface: A traditional singalong in England performed sometime in mid-July.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rendered' rearranges ENGLAND SAY, and 'around' wraps that round UL, the 'middle of' July.
explanation.definitionFit: This Scots song by Burns is the traditional one sung in chorus at New Year, so it is a classic communal chorus.

clue.text: Show up a House of Lords member, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly says the phrase is to be heard rather than read, giving a word that sounds alike

parts.note: a peer is a member of the House of Lords, so this is 'a peer'

explanation.surface: A member of the upper house is said to have arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: The House of Lords is the upper chamber of the UK parliament, whose members are peers.
explanation.definitionFit: To show up is to arrive or become visible, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Key story that may not be true

definitions.meaning: the table on a map explaining its symbols

definitions.text: story that may not be true

explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' is the explanation printed on a map, not a lock opener.
explanation.definitionFit: The panel decoding a map's symbols and a traditional tale of doubtful truth share this word.

clue.text: Drunk back by hotel? Nonsense

indicators.note: back means the word for a drunk is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A drinker returns to a hotel and talks rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the word for a drunkard; 'by' simply places the hotel letter beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is British slang for rubbish or foolish talk, a straight synonym for nonsense.

clue.text: Content to leave etching as an illustration

definitions.meaning: remove the inside letters of etching and you are left with E and G, the Latin abbreviation e.g., whose English meaning is this phrase
by way of a typical instance

explanation.surface: Someone is happy to keep an engraving as a picture in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' looks like happy, but it means the inside of 'etching'; taking that out leaves EG, read as the abbreviation e.g. and expanded into English.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving an illustration is offering an instance, which is what this everyday phrase introduces.

clue.text: Go in for chips without carp

indicators.note: without means the fish's name is taken away from the start of the word

parts.note: Chips is the traditional nickname for a ship's carpenter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Choose a portion of fries rather than the fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chips' is not fries but the old naval nickname for a carpenter; 'without' strips CARP from CARPENTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To go in is to come into a place, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Dispute low temperature

parts.note: to low is to moo like a cow

explanation.surface: An argument about the weather turning cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' is not small but the sound a cow makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A point open to argument is debatable, and as a verb the word means raise for discussion.

clue.text: Song couple heard with others in Bury

parts.note: a lay is a short song or ballad

indicators.note: heard says the number meaning a pair is said aloud, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a couple is two
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: A duet is listened to along with other music in the Lancashire town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury looks like the town in Lancashire, England, but it is the verb meaning to inter.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter a body after death is expressed by this gentle idiom.

clue.text: Gobble suet regularly, getting very overweight

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, every other one in each word

explanation.surface: Eating lots of fatty pudding filling often will make you very fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes alternate letters: OBE from gObBlE and SE from SuEt. Suet is hard animal fat used in British puddings.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical term for being heavier than is healthy, a direct synonym for very fat.

clue.text: Exam's first question was worrying, second is deemed comparable

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word Exam's

parts.note: ate, as in 'what ate him?', means troubled or worried

explanation.surface: A student found the opening question of an exam troubling, and the next one similar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was worrying' gives ATE, as in 'something ate at him'.
explanation.definitionFit: When one thing is treated as equal or equivalent to another, it corresponds to it, matching the sense of being judged alike.

clue.text: Went to bed exhausted following ride I'd taken

indicators.note: following means the word for exhausted comes after the shortened ride
taken means those letters are removed from the word ride

parts.note: exhausted means tired

explanation.surface: Someone went to sleep worn out after a ride they had been on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken' removes the letters of I'd from ride, and 'following' places the word for exhausted after what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw for the night is a formal way of saying someone went to sleep.
